items.content:
Earlier gameplay summary (agent-written, uncertain claims remain uncertain):
Current run: Act 1 Ironclad. Last verified screen before the latest input was an empty “Loot!” panel with Proceed visible after completing floor 5. Verified stats: 39/80 HP, 161 gold, 15-card deck, no potions. Deck includes starter Strikes, Defends, Bash, unplayable Ascender’s Bane, plus Inflame, Iron Wave, Sword Boomerang, and newly added Impervious. Latest completed input clicked Proceed at (0.867,0.700); its result has not been observed.

Controls/observed mechanics: Drag attacks onto enemies and skills onto the player; E ends turn. Clicking blank space during enemy turns/transitions was used to wait for animations. Hand cards enlarge and shift after hovering or other plays; several old-coordinate drags failed or played the wrong card, including Defend instead of Strike. Verify the settled card title/center and energy after every play. Some inputs were rejected as stale_observation and had no effect. Potions are used from the top bar by clicking the flask, then Drink. The bottom-left book opens Draw Pile. Gold and card rewards are separate entries; Proceed follows reward collection. Completed combats have repeatedly healed 6 HP afterward.

Card evidence: Defend grants 5 Block. Inflame costs 1 and grants 2 Strength for the rest of combat. Normally it raised Strike from 6 to 8 damage. Bash costs 2 and applied 2 Vulnerable in earlier fights. Iron Wave costs 1, grants 5 Block, and deals attack damage. During Weakened, Strength-boosted Strike dealt 6 and Bash dealt 7; a Strike against a Vulnerable target dealt 9. After Weakened expired, Strike again dealt 8. One Iron Wave under those combat conditions was observed dealing 5 damage and granting 5 Block. Sword Boomerang reads 3 damage to a random enemy three times; it remains untested, including whether Strength affects every hit. Impervious reads: costs 2, gain 30 Block, Exhaust; it has not been used.

Earlier route/history: First enemy gave 20 gold and Inflame. At The Cleric, Heal cost 35 and Remove cost 50; Leave was chosen without spending. Jaw Worm (43 HP) died on turn 4, giving 19 gold and Iron Wave. Two Lice followed: a misfired Bash left the first at 1 HP and led to a 15-damage enemy turn. The surviving Louse used Curl Up, observed gaining 8 Block once after first taking attack damage, and gained 3 Strength. Rewards were 13 gold, an Energy Potion, and Sword Boomerang, leaving 151 gold and 57 HP before the Slimes.

Slime combat: Five Slimes initially intended 26 total damage. Energy Potion raised energy from 3 to 5/3. All five were eventually defeated over six turns. Bash→Strike efficiently killed a 1-HP Slime after Vulnerable; Inflame was played mid-combat. Acid Slimes applied 2 Weakened, observed as 25% less attack damage. Multi-enemy intents included attacks and debuffs; defensive turns with Defends/Iron Wave successfully blocked visible attacks. An intended second Strike once played Defend instead, leaving the player to take 9 damage that enemy turn. Combat ended at 33/80 HP, then post-combat healing raised it to 39/80. Rewards were 10 gold and a card choice. Impervious was selected over Dark Embrace and Dual Wield; gold rose to 161 and deck count to 15.

Current navigation issue: After collecting all floor-5 rewards, Proceed displayed a map with a bottom-left Return button. The completed lower enemy node had one visible connected enemy node directly above it at approximately (0.296,0.764). Repeated clicks on that upper node only highlighted it; no encounter loaded. Return and later Escape each brought back the empty Loot! screen with Proceed. Proceed reopened the map, but further node clicks again only highlighted it. The latest Proceed click may have reopened the map, but this is unverified. It remains unclear whether this is a map overlay, a confirmation issue, or another required UI step; do not assume travel occurred.

Active goals: Resolve the floor-5 loot/map state, enter the connected upper enemy encounter, preserve HP, then collect rewards and continue along the visible route. The upper route was previously thought to lead toward an elite, but that remains uncertain.
